title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 3
text: When I returned to the village from the dark side of this world.
“Big bro, big bro! Welcome back!”

The moment I got back to the village, Keel came running up to me. Lately, you’ve been greeting me like a dog whenever I come home, haven’t you? You’re turning into a loyal dog. And to think, you used to glare at me with eyes like a dog that had been abandoned and lost all trust in humans. With that thought, I gave Keel a light pat on the head, half in exasperation.
“I’m home.”
“Welcome home, Naofumi-sama.”
“I’m home. Raphtalia, has anything changed?”
“Not really… but—”
“Big bro! Big bro!”
“Keel, I’m talking to Raphtalia. Keep it down for a bit, or go chase a ball or tend to the crepe tree or something.”
“Big bro, big bro! There’s a new flavor of crepe fruit! It’s chocolate batter with chocolate sauce! Perfect for Valentine’s Day, right?”
Keel completely ignored my words, said whatever he wanted to say, and showed me the chocolate-flavored crepe. A chocolate-flavored crepe, huh… Feels like we’ve really taken things to the extreme.
“Yes, I was just about to report that to Naofumi-sama.”

Ah, so Raphtalia was also going to report on the chocolate-flavored crepes. I wonder if this really is something worth reporting? Well, even small changes can sometimes lead to problems, so I suppose it’s necessary.
“Hmm… So they do celebrate Valentine’s Day here after all.”

Since they have Christmas and New Year’s, I figured it was possible. Plus, I’ve been hearing talk about it in business circles lately. Apparently, even if prices go up a bit, plenty of people still buy them, so it’s a prime season for business. Accessory merchants and others were making a fuss about whether or not to venture into business areas beyond their usual scope.
“Yes, it’s here. Everyone in the village is talking about it right now, too.”
“So chocolate exists in this world, too?”

Did they recreate it from a plant similar to the cacao tree? It sounds like something a past hero might have popularized. …Or maybe other reincarnated people. It grates on me, but their efforts do end up being useful in one way or another.
“Yes. From what I’ve been able to find out, there’s apparently a tree in a certain region that bears chocolate, and I hear it’s commonly traded around this time of year.”
“Huh…”
A tree that bears chocolate… I wonder if that refers to the finished product?

It sounds like a story I’ve heard somewhere before, I thought, glancing over at the bread tree and the crepe tree. I’d better not ask who invented them or where they came from. I’d definitely step on a landmine.

Come to think of it, I’ve heard that story too. I thought they were talking about cacao, but the moment I heard the term “chocolate farmer,” I had a vague inkling. Just like our creepy trees, I bet they actually grow chocolate. Maybe the crepe tree will eventually be called a “crepe farmer” too… To be honest, I really don’t want that.
“So? Are you planning to celebrate Valentine’s Day in the village too?”
“You’re quick on the uptake, big bro!”
“Well, I learned my lesson at Christmas, after all.”
It was a huge hassle, but seeing everyone so happy didn’t make me feel bad about it.
“So? Is Valentine’s Day definitely just an event where girls give chocolate to the guys they like?”
“Is there any other kind?”

……I can’t tell him. The fact that, back in the day, I used to take advantage of events like this to go on a chocolate spree. I’d say things like, “There’s such a thing as ‘friend chocolate,’ right?” and hand them out to everyone—men and women alike—without distinction. It didn’t matter if it was in real life or online. I loved every single event and was totally into it! I was.
“Also… Melty-chan has come to make a proposal.”
Melty? It feels like it’s been a while since I’ve seen her. Has it been since Christmas? Well, she was asleep back then, though.
“A proposal?”
“She’s suggesting, ‘How about selling chocolate as part of Filo-chan’s idol activities?’ The idea is to use the proceeds for reconstruction funds.”

With that, Melty arrived alongside Filo in her human form. That’s right. While Melty is busy with diplomacy in various countries, Filo is busy with her idol career—singing and dancing. Currently, Filo is the village’s top breadwinner—mainly through her idol activities and merchandise sales. There’s a device called an “audio crystal” that plays music, similar to a “video crystal.” Well, those are on the pricier side, but there are also cheaper options—like gramophones—that play record-like discs.
“Hmm? The chocolate’s sooo gooood!”
With chocolate sauce smeared all over her cheeks, Filo was devouring a crepe. But seriously, can’t she do something about that pronunciation?
“It’s under the guise of ‘homemade chocolate made by Filo-chan,’ you see.”
“Can Filo even make chocolate by hand?”

I mean, I don’t think Filo is the type to cook—she’s strictly on the eating side, not the cooking side. I’ve never even seen her cook in the first place. Usually, the staff at the shop makes it, or sometimes I do. If she’s going to eat it herself, she’d probably just eat it raw.
“Well… you’re right. But we don’t really need to prove that Filo-chan made it, do we?”
“I guess you’re right.”
Melty, you’re pretty shady yourself, aren’t you? Fans want Valentine’s Day gifts from their idols that the idols actually made themselves, right? I guess this is just how reality works, though.
“I think we could make a good profit if Naofumi and the kids here produced and sold them.”
“That’s not a bad idea. It seems like we were planning to hold a Valentine’s Day event anyway.”
“Exactly! So, could you help us out?”
“Yeah, yeah, I get it. So? How are we going to process the chocolate?”
“I was thinking of leaving that to the national chef, but can you handle it, Naofumi?”
“Bro, hurry up and give it a taste already.”
“I can do it, but… Hey, Keel, enough about the chocolate crepes—you need to join us, too. It’s part of our idol activities.”
“Whaaaaaat!?”
Keel was so startled she almost dropped her crepe. Don’t drop it and freak out again. Ren isn’t here right now, after all.
“What are you so surprised about? It’s a great opportunity. If we beat Filo in sales, you can stop wearing that outfit.”
“W-well, I guess so…”
Keel is still being forced to wear feminine outfits he doesn’t want—maid costumes with frills and dresses. Of course, he takes them off when he’s in dog form.
“Your sales performance has been pretty good. An idol debut wouldn’t be so bad, right?”
“N-no way, big bro! I can’t sing in front of that many people! I’m not that good anyway.”
……Hmph. I placed my hand on Keel’s shoulder with a gentle gaze—though inwardly I was sneering—and, bringing myself down to his eye level, spoke.

“It’ll be fine, Keel. Being an idol isn’t about having people listen to your singing—it’s a job where you show them you can sing and dance, and sell them the right to be in a place where they can see you do it.”
“It feels like you’re teaching him something completely wrong!”
Raphtalia interjects, but I’m not wrong, am I? Whether you’re a good singer or not doesn’t matter.
“Is that so? When I look at Filo-chan, it feels different to me.”
“Hmm? Is that so?”

“Filo is… in a league of her own. She’s the kind of idol who can charge money just for singing. There are different kinds of idols. Not every idol has to be like Filo. Besides… people are starting to get tired of just Filo.”
“Boo!”
“What did you say, Naofumi! Correct yourself!”

Filo and Melty protest, but… at least as far as I know, most idols disappear from the industry within ten years. At best, only those who’ve managed to transition into acting actually survive. Well, that’s just how it is with the entertainment business. It’s not just Filo—even Keel needs to make money while she can, or she won’t turn a profit.

Keel seems to have a steady, low-key following, after all. Her fan base is probably different, so there’s no reason she can’t pull it off. Actually, positioning her as a rival would be the smart move.

As for Motoyasu’s trio… they overlap with Filo’s category. They’re rivals who can sing and dance—and since there are three of them, they each have their own personality, but they can’t beat the real deal. So compared to Filo, they’re a bit lackluster.

Plus, all the profits go into Motoyasu’s pocket. Why should I have to do something that doesn’t put money in my own pocket? …Well, Motoyasu does pour all the profits back into Filo, though. Come to think of it, Motoyasu’s a pretty shady guy, too.

Back to Keel. This guy looks good in men’s clothes, too. When she dresses as a woman, she comes across as innocent and fresh. So, if we go with the “male disguise” route—the “Takarazuka-style” approach—it might actually work out.
“For now… as an exception, let’s dress her in men’s clothes as a ‘beautiful woman in men’s attire.’”
“It feels kind of annoying when you order me around like that, big bro.”
“What? You don’t want to wear them? I’m not sure about a fundoshi, though.”
“That’s not it! Even though I’m dressed as a guy, I feel like I haven’t changed at all!”
Well, that makes sense. Being androgynous is different from being a man. I’m no Tailor, but it seems like there are a lot of people in this world who are interested in subculture, too.
“Hey, Naofumi! Fix this already!”
“If you want me to, you’ll have to prove yourself. Her Majesty Queen Melty, producer and background vocalist. If Filo’s still an idol ten years from now, I’ll correct it for you.”
“Just you wait and see!”
Well, that “correction” will probably just end with a single phrase: “Wow, that’s impressive.”

Philo and Melty are still getting along great, as always. All things considered, it seems Melty sings with her from time to time. So, for all intents and purposes, there’s no problem with Melty being the idol.

However, there’s a major issue with Melty. That is, she is Her Majesty the Queen of Melromarc, which has become the world’s greatest superpower. Because of her position as queen, if she gets too carried away with her idol career, it could cause problems elsewhere. It could lead to the world’s queen being looked down upon.
“For now, let’s have Imiya or a Tailor make Keel’s outfit.”
…A Tailor would probably know more about this sort of thing. In a fujoshi sort of way.
“Aaaah… Even Keel-kun has fallen victim to Lord Naofumi’s scheme.”

Raphtalia groans, clutching her head. I don’t know about that. This is for the village’s development, and ultimately, for the good of the world. Besides… he’s practically already fallen victim to it, isn’t he? Especially since he’s clinging to me like a dog.
“Ugh… I don’t want to sing and dance.”
“It’ll be fine, Keel.”
“What will be fine?”

“In your case, it’s less about singing and dancing and more like putting on a play. I’ll ask someone who seems to know about choreography to handle that, so just act like you’re selling stuff as a traveling merchant, exactly as you’re told.”
“Is that right, big bro?”
“Yeah.”
“Then I’ll do my best!”
Keel started wagging his tail, showing his enthusiasm. He’s such a pushover.
“By the way, big bro. It’s about chocolate.”
Keel joined Raphtalia in staring at me. Actually, Melty and everyone else in the village is looking my way, too. Are they still going to keep bringing this up?
“What is it?”
“They want you to teach them how to make delicious homemade chocolate.”

…So that’s how it is. Well, I do serve dessert, but I’ve never taught anyone how to make delicious chocolate. So, it’s Valentine’s Day, and the girls in the village are all fired up… is that it? Come to think of it… every year, I used to have a bunch of friends who wanted “friend chocolates.” I wonder if they’re doing okay?
